one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked knowledge of how to properly install rstan 2.32.7 with pinned dependencies on Linux, failed to get rstan working, and then substituted a cascade of off-spec tools (cmdstanpy, brms, Python method-of-moments) before prematurely declaring completion.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 attempts to install cmdstanr (the wrong package) from a non-standard repo with type='binary' (unsupported on Linux), demonstrating the agent lacks knowledge of how to correctly install the required rstan 2.32.7 package.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16 marks explicit pivot to Python workarounds ('Since RStan is not available... I'll solve this by creating a PyStan solution'), abandoning rstan installation entirely and writing off-spec Python method-of-moments code, making failure irreversible.
t_surface_evidence: Step 7 output: 'Error in library(rstan) : there is no package called rstan' — clear observable failure signal confirming rstan is not installed.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge about installing rstan 2.32.7 on Linux: it tried the wrong package (cmdstanr), then tried rstan without pinning the required version (2.32.7) or configuring Makevars/compatible dependencies (StanHeaders, BH, Rcpp, RcppEigen). This knowledge gap caused the installation to fail, triggering a cascade of off-spec substitutions.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: 'type binary is not supported on this platform' error. Step 7: 'Error in library(rstan): there is no package called rstan'. Step 12: 'No stan packages found'. These signals appeared before t_commit=16.
